answer: Payment sits in escrow until a jury grades the work, and a replayed submission claws the whole payment back to the pool. A farm therefore fronts the cost of every answer and earns nothing when the copy is caught. A recruiter cannot audit its own recruit either, so each new identity needs a second independent grader, which doubles the headcount a farm has to maintain. On a tundra of cheap aliases the escrow is the only real cost, and it lands before any revenue. A lagoon of clones looks calm until the first clawback drains it. The terrace is narrow: one replay and the batch pays zero.
